lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Today, we pull the plug on some nodes.
What happens to your jobs when a node crashes, hangs or reboots? With sind power, you find out on purpose, and watch Slurm react.
Shutdown and reboot let systemd stop a node cleanly. Cut and cycle kill it at once, like pulling the plug.
Power on starts it again. And freeze suspends all its processes: Docker still lists the node as running, but it stops responding.
Say your cluster has four workers. Run sind power cut on all of them, and they're gone in an instant.
sind power on starts them again, and points their DNS records at their current addresses.
Now freeze worker zero. It ignores SSH and Slurm alike.
Later, sind power unfreeze lets it carry on.
Slurm notices a lost node only when it stops answering pings. It shows as idle star first, and as down about five minutes later.
Once slurmd registers again, after unfreeze or power on, the node returns to service by itself.
Five minutes is a long wait in a test. So set a shorter slurmd timeout, in the main section of your cluster config.
slurmctld pings about every third of the timeout, so a lost worker now goes down within about thirty to forty seconds.
So: each power action is a Docker operation, Slurm spots lost nodes through missed pings, and a lower timeout makes tests quick.
Now go break something, on purpose! Next up: Diagnostics. See you there!
